summary: Lid sensor firmware reset during depot repair breaks hibernate and prevents Intune check-in
description: Issue summary: After depot battery replacement on a small subset of fleet laptops, the embedded lid sensor controller firmware is intermittently resetting. When the controller resets, Windows fails to enter and resume reliably from hibernate, and the provisioning agent does not complete Intune MDM check-in on first boot. Impact: Affected devices do not check in with Intune for up to 30 minutes after repair, preventing policy push and automated asset tagging. Users report black-screen/resume loops when closing and opening lids. Scope: 7 devices reported in staging pool (Dell and Lenovo variants); no customer-facing devices confirmed yet. Temporary workaround: Avoid hibernate; use full shutdown or disable lid-to-sleep until firmware backport is deployed. Attachments: dump collection archive (attached to ticket), serial numbers list, depot repair notes.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Reproduce from depot image flow: wipe device and apply standard depot image (Windows 11 23H2 gold image).
2) Perform battery replacement flow per depot SOP (disconnect main battery, reseat internal lid cable, reflash EC if prompted).
3) Boot to OOBE, complete autopilot stage and provisioning-agent runs.
4) Close lid to trigger hibernate/suspend, open lid to attempt resume.
5) Observe Intune check-in status in Company Portal / MDM logs (Event Viewer / AAD Device Registration).
observed_behavior:
- On affected devices the embedded lid controller logs show a reset during the battery reseat step.
- Windows enters an unstable hibernate: on resume the display remains black and a 'Hardware interrupted' entry appears in System Event Log.
- Provisioning agent stalls at 'Completing device setup' and Intune status remains 'Not checked in' for ~15-30 minutes.
- 'pnputil' shows lid sensor HID instance path flapping (device removal/arrival).
expected_behavior: Lid sensor remains stable after battery replacement, hibernate/resume works reliably, and device completes Intune check-in during initial provisioning within normal window (~2-5 minutes).

investigation_notes: Initial triage (Aisha): collected dumps from three affected devices and correlated with depot repair logs; firmware update/EC reflash performed in 5 of 7 repairs.
SRE (J. Park): kernel logs show ACPI lid device detaching and re-attaching right after battery reseat; presence of EC watchdog reset correlated with power rail brownout events.

Firmware team (L. Chen): reproduced EC lid-controller reset on bench when Vbat momentarily dips below threshold during cable reseat; candidate fix prepared in EC branch 'lid-power-stability' — PR #312.

Provisioning (M. Rivera): provisioning-agent assumes stable device enumeration; device-flap triggers a long backoff around install tasks which delays Intune check-in; code path PR #198 adds a faster re-enqueue on HID re-detect.

Hypothesis: transient Vbat dip during battery replacement triggers EC watchdog -> lid controller resets -> HID device re-enumeration -> provisioning agent backoff delays MDM check-in and causes hibernate/resume instability.
Telemetry note: power-rail brownouts only observed on depot bench A/C adapters with older firmware on Dell 7480 and on one Lenovo unit with 3rd-party battery pack.
Customer risk assessment: medium for internal fleet repairs; high if same pattern occurs in customer depot repairs where repair SOP is identical.
comments: Aisha Kumar (Support) [2026-03-10]: Created ticket after three staging devices failed Intune check-in post-battery-replacement. Attached serials and dmp files.
L. Chen (Firmware) [2026-03-11]: Confirmed EC watchdog timeline. Built candidate EC firmware image and validated on bench with deliberate Vbat dip — lid controller remained stable in 20/20 runs.
Marco Rivera (Provisioning) [2026-03-11]: Instrumented provisioning-agent to skip long backoff on HID reattach in dev; local test reduced check-in latency to ~45s. Preparing PR and test matrix.
SRE (Jordan Park) [2026-03-12]: Suggested adding post-repair validation step to depot SOP: run 'powercfg /a' and 'Get-PnpDevice -PresentOnly' to confirm lid HID presence before sealing device.
Aisha Kumar (Support) [2026-03-12]: Rolling temporary SOP to depot techs to avoid hibernate and prefer shutdown until firmware backport is staged.
workarounds:
- Depot technicians: after battery replacement, perform a full shutdown instead of hibernate to avoid resume loop.
- If provisioning stalls, manually trigger 'dsregcmd /status' and restart the provisioning-agent service; that often forces immediate recheck.
- Use repository EC image 'lid-power-stability' for test benches only until sign-off.
next_steps:
1) Firmware: backport EC patch to stable branch and push internal test build (target ETA 2026-03-16).
2) Provisioning: merge expedited HID reattach handler and release hotfix to staging (target ETA 2026-03-14).
3) Ops: update depot SOP with post-repair verification steps and communicate temporary workaround to depot teams.
4) After fixes, run 100 repair cycle validation on both Dell and Lenovo models in staging.
resolution_notes: Triage complete. Blocking fixes identified in firmware and provisioning-agent. No full rollback applied; awaiting firmware backport and provisioning hotfix. Post-fix validation plan drafted.
